source.title: A Minimal ReLU Classifier on Non-Linearly Separable Data: Convergence and Implicit Bias at and beyond the Edge of Stability
source.authors: Quan Nguyen; Robin Yadav; Param Mody; Mark Schmidt

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests gradient-descent training error and failure conditions in a minimal ReLU classification model and MNIST experiments, using theoretical analysis and empirical runs rather than the benchmark and architecture settings in most claim versions.
record.gate_note: Its main theoretical setting is a tied two-neuron ReLU network on three non-linearly separable points, not CIFAR or random labels. It also reports an unsymmetric four-parameter result and MNIST experiments. Prior-work results in the introduction and related work are not rows. The reported initialization and learning-rate conditions, dead-region failures, and MNIST outcomes are included.
record.test_reason: The study tests V5's large-step recovery and full-batch stability question using a minimal ReLU classifier with logistic loss. Its convergence and catapult results extend that question beyond the original settings. It does not test V1's convolutional-network classification claim or V2–V4 and V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors establish conditional convergence and explicit implicit bias in a minimal logistic ReLU classifier, finite-update catapult recovery, and convergence with growing adaptive steps. MNIST provides finite-time evidence of analogous switching and loss decay; it does not establish asymptotic MNIST loss laws.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a tied two-neuron ReLU classifier on a three-point non-linearly separable dataset, with logistic loss and full-batch GD; it also runs two-layer 16-unit MNIST experiments. This differs from the benchmark and architecture recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome depends on whether initialization lies in the active cone or dead/linear regions, and on step-size conditions and schedules. For the MNIST 4-versus-7 experiments, seven trained-output runs with η≥0.02 end with every hidden unit inactive; random initialization schedule results differ substantially across schedules.

fits_no_version.finding: Toy-model convergence, dead-region trapping, stationary initializations, and local convergence after removing weight symmetry.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Successful optimization of this minimal ReLU classifier depends on activation-region geometry and initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: Two matched MNIST runs attain 100% training accuracy; a separate 30-run experiment yields 23 fits and seven fully inactive endpoints.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small fully connected ReLU classifiers can fit binary MNIST, while some trained-output runs terminate with dead hidden units.

fits_no_version.finding: Weight-proportional adaptive steps accelerate loss decay, while more aggressive adaptive schedules can leave the active cone.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive learning-rate convergence in this classifier depends on the schedule and initialization.

record.problems: The theoretical results concern a highly specific three-point, one-dimensional dataset and a two-neuron tied model. MNIST reports one matched pair of 3-versus-5 runs and does not quantify variability across initializations; the 4-versus-7 experiment details differ from the 3-versus-5 setup described in Section 7. The seven inactive-run outcomes do not report final training error.
record.rows_left_out: No otherwise qualifying result rows left out. Prior-work claims cited in the Introduction and Related Work were excluded because they are not results of this study.

untested.parts: All: no convolutional CIFAR-10/100 training experiments, random-label tests, or relevant model-size and training-recipe comparisons.
All: no teacher-student width sweep or spurious-minimum frequency comparison.
All: no depth or shortcut comparison.
All: no activation-matched initialization comparison measuring speed or trainable depth.

Wide squared-loss networks; the initial linearized-model stability limit; curvature reduction during recovery; a larger-rate divergence boundary in that setting; prolonged sharpness hovering near the threshold; and divergence despite starting below it.
All: no normalization comparison or Fixup experiment.

missing.what: Explicit above-threshold convergence conditions: Remark C.2 gives two initialization families with initial sharpness greater than 2/η while cone invariance and loss convergence hold.
missing.locator: Remark C.2; Corollary C.1; Theorems 4.2 and 4.5

missing.what: Progressive sharpening from below 2/η through a finite-time crossing, with convergence guaranteed by cone invariance. This establishes crossing, not prolonged hovering.
missing.locator: Theorem C.4 and its proof; Figure 1(b–c)

missing.what: Expanded catapult initialization range: when 0<ν<1/3, loss becomes exponentially small after five updates, with all five iterates remaining in the cone.
Post-catapult empirical persistence: η=16,64,256,1024 runs remain in the cone through 3,000 steps; for η=64,256,1024, second-update log10 losses are −3.29, −13.80, −55.85.

record.verdict_notes: Different architecture or loss alone is not a negative verdict. The toy and MNIST failures do not challenge V1, and adaptive-schedule failures do not challenge V5's fixed-step claims. No original-source exclusion applies to this study.

versions.untested_parts: No CIFAR-10/100 benchmarks, corrupted or random labels, Adam, smaller-model sweep, early stopping, or regularized recipes are tested. The theoretical toy model is not a sufficiently large convolutional network.
No two-layer teacher-student neuron-count comparison or spurious-local-minimum frequency sweep.
No depth sweep comparing plain and residual networks.
No initialization comparison for training speed or depth; MNIST initialization is stated but not varied.
The paper tests large-step loss behavior on its toy network, not the wide squared-loss networks, full-batch sharpness trajectories, or divergence conditions described in this version.
No batch-normalization comparison; MNIST experiments report fixed learning rate and no normalization comparison.

rows.subject: two-neuron ReLU network, symmetric weights ±w and output weights fixed at 1
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent with constant step size on summed logistic loss, initialized in the active cone under stated invariance conditions.
rows.note: The theorem gives an upper bound conditional on remaining in the active cone; it does not state an exact finite-time classification error.
rows.check: The bound concerns the time average of summed training logistic losses. Remark C.2 explicitly establishes that admissible conditions include initialization above the local sharpness threshold; record those conditions separately. This is not evidence about V1's CNNs.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.1, Theorem 4.2; Corollary C.1; Remark C.2.

rows.subject: two-neuron ReLU network, symmetric weights ±w and output weights fixed at 1
rows.operation_detail: Constant-step gradient descent from an active-cone initialization that remains there.
rows.note: The paper derives vanishing loss and max-margin directional convergence for trajectories that stay in C.
rows.check: The asymptotic convergence result includes constant-step trajectories starting above the local sharpness threshold under Remark C.2. It does not establish prolonged threshold hovering or V1.

rows.subject: two-neuron ReLU network, symmetric weights ±w and output weights fixed at 1
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent initialized in the dead region, where the trajectory is trapped.
rows.note: The model cannot reach zero loss from this initialization; the dead region is invariant.
rows.check: Dead-region failure in a tied two-neuron classifier does not measure any stated version. It cannot qualify V1's sufficiently large CNN claim.

rows.subject: two-neuron ReLU network, symmetric weights ±w and output weights fixed at 1
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent from stationary or invariant initializations outside the active cone.
rows.measure: Whether the trajectory enters the active cone
rows.value: Stationary initialization stays fixed; w0=0 implies wt=0 for all t, precluding entry into C
rows.note: The result shows that not every non-dead initialization is guaranteed to reach the active cone.
rows.check: Cone-entry obstructions in this toy architecture do not test any stated version.

rows.subject: two-neuron ReLU network, symmetric weights ±w and output weights fixed at 1
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent initialized in the linear region, then enters and remains in the active cone under the lemma's conditions.
rows.value: Finite time τ exists with θt∈C for all t≥τ; subsequent loss has the Theorem 4.2 bound
rows.note: A stated sufficient-condition result for entry from the linear region.
rows.check: Finite-time cone entry and subsequent convergence do not, as recorded, establish a stability-threshold trajectory. The architecture and dataset also fall outside V1.

rows.subject: two-neuron ReLU network, symmetric weights ±w and output weights fixed at 1
rows.operation_detail: Constant-step GD from a specified active-cone initialization, with step size taken sufficiently large.
rows.measure: Loss after first and second updates
rows.baseline: Initial loss does not depend on η
rows.note: The paper describes a first-update loss spike followed by exponentially small loss after the second update; iterates remain in C through those updates.
rows.check: This measures catapult-like loss recovery with logistic loss in a narrow network. The guarantee covers the first two updates, not indefinite convergence, curvature reduction, or the squared-loss divergence boundary.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5.1, Theorem 5.1 and following discussion; Appendix E, Proposition E.1.

rows.measure: Average training logistic loss and endpoint weight growth
rows.note: A provable convergence bound under the specified adaptive schedule.
rows.check: Convergence under a growing adaptive schedule does not establish recovery above a measured stability threshold or fixed-step edge-of-stability dynamics.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU network, trained output layer
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent run on MNIST that ended with every hidden unit inactive on every image.

conditions.value: MNIST digits 3 and 5; Section H.1 notes 256 training examples

rows.measure: Final classification outcome and hidden-unit activity
rows.value: Every hidden unit inactive on every image at end; no run ends with a misclassified image and a live unit
rows.note: Seven runs end inactive; the text does not give their final training error, and says no run ends with a misclassified image and a live unit. The outcomes support the dead-region boundary behavior, but do not quantify training error for these runs.
rows.check: H.1 identifies these as MNIST 4-versus-7 runs with 32 images per class and 30,000 steps, not the 256-example 3-versus-5 experiment. All seven failures have trained output layers and learning rates at least 0.02. These outcomes do not test V1.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU network, trained output layer
rows.operation_detail: MNIST gradient-descent runs; reported aggregate count of runs that fit the data and then remained in active cones.
rows.measure: Runs fitting the data and remaining in active cones thereafter
rows.value: 23 of 30 fit the data and thereafter remained in active cones
rows.note: This is an aggregate count across 30 runs. The section 7 count does not specify every run's configuration; H.1 gives the detailed experiment as 15 fixed-output and 15 trained-output runs on MNIST 4-versus-7, with differing stated run outcomes.
rows.check: The aggregate comprises 15 fixed-output and 15 trained-output runs on MNIST 4 versus 7, with 64 images and 30,000 steps. All 15 fixed-output runs and eight trained-output runs fit by step 32. The subject incorrectly describes all 30 as trained-output runs; Section 7's dataset description conflicts with H.1.

rows.subject: two-neuron ReLU network, symmetric weights ±w and output weights fixed at 1
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on 20 random initializations with three step-size schedules.

conditions.value: 20 initializations in C; |w0|=10U, U∼Unif[−1.3,0.7], random sign, b0∼Unif(−|w0|,|w0|), g0∼Unif[−3,3], seed 0

rows.measure: Runs staying in C; median and maximum log10 final loss
rows.note: The paper says median and largest final losses coincide to two decimals, consistent with empirical scaling 5/(t log t); κ=1/2 is outside Theorem 5.3's range.
rows.check: Adaptive-schedule cone retention and final loss do not measure a stability threshold or any other stated version. The initialization magnitude is 10 raised to U, not 10 multiplied by U.

rows.subject: two-neuron ReLU network, symmetric weights ±w and output weights fixed at 1
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on 20 random initializations using the loss-adaptive schedule.
rows.measure: Runs staying in C; median and maximum log10 final loss
rows.note: Two failures start outside both sufficient invariance conditions and enter D within two steps; with η0=0.25 both runs stay in C.
rows.check: Failure of two loss-adaptive runs to retain the cone does not test V5's constant-step recovery or divergence claims.

rows.subject: two-neuron ReLU network, symmetric weights ±w and output weights fixed at 1
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on 20 random initializations with step size squared proportional to weight magnitude.
rows.measure: Runs staying in C; median and maximum log10 final loss
rows.note: Every run leaves the active cone; the table reports the median and maximum final log10 loss.
rows.check: Failure under a squared-weight adaptive schedule does not establish divergence under V5's fixed learning-rate conditions.
